title: Fabrication, characterization and herbicidal mechanism of a β-cyclodextrin-cassia oil bio-based nanoherbicide against  Taraxacum mongolicum
content: Conventional chemical herbicides have caused escalating herbicide resistance and environmental contamination. Plant-derived essential oils emerge as promising eco-friendly alternatives, yet their field application is constrained by poor water solubility, high volatility and limited persistence. Herein, a bio-based nanoherbicide, β-cyclodextrin-cassia oil (β-CD-CA), was developed via ultrasonic-assisted inclusion encapsulation. The preparation parameters were systematically optimized, and its physicochemical properties, herbicidal efficacy, in planta translocation and underlying mechanisms were comprehensively evaluated against Taraxacum mongolicum. Under optimal conditions, β-CD-CA nanoparticles achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 72.95% with an average particle size of 225.3 nm, featuring a regular rhombic morphology and excellent dispersibility. Further characterization demonstrated that the nanoparticles possessed excellent sustained-release properties, with a cumulative release rate of only 53% at 72 h in the emulsion state; in powder form, the encapsulation efficiency decreased by less than 5% after 30 days of storage at 4 °C in the dark. Herbicidal bioassays confirmed that β-CD-CA completely inhibited seed germination of T. mongolicum, with an EC50 of 4.39 g L−1, lower than that of free CA, verifying that nanoencapsulation enhanced herbicidal efficacy with reduced dosage. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that β-CD-CA exerted phytotoxicity via disrupting cell membrane integrity, inducing oxidative stress and inhibiting photosynthesis. RhB-based tracing verified its bidirectional translocation through xylem-mediated acropetal and phloem-mediated basipetal transport. Untargeted metabolomics further revealed that β-CD-CA triggered extensive metabolic reprogramming, redirecting metabolic flux from growth-related primary metabolism to stress-defensive secondary metabolism. This work provides a feasible strategy for eco-friendly nanoherbicide development and novel insights into their herbicidal mechanisms.
